lesson.title: Comparing Volume Reports

sections.title: Recorded Volumes at Noon
sections.content: There are two different reports regarding the volume of a cup at noon. Report A states the cup held 70 mL. Report B states the cup held 90 mL.

sections.title: Unresolved Differences
sections.content: The two reports provide different measurements for the same object at the same time. Because neither report has precedence, it is not established which measurement is correct or why they differ.

lesson.summary: Two reports show different volumes for a cup at noon: 70 mL and 90 mL. Neither report is considered more authoritative than the other.

vocabulary.definition: A unit used to measure volume.
The right or status of being more important or correct than something else.

discussion_questions: What is the volume listed in Report A?

Does one report have more authority than the other?

lesson.title: Understanding One Quarter

sections.title: What is a Quarter?
sections.content: A quarter means taking one group of things and dividing it into four equal parts. When you have four equal parts together, each part is called a quarter.

sections.title: Example: Counters
sections.content: If you have twelve counters, one quarter of those counters is three counters. This is because twelve divided into four equal groups gives you three in each group.

lesson.summary: A quarter is one of four equal parts that make up a whole. For example, if you divide twelve items into four equal groups, each group contains three items.

vocabulary.definition: One of four equal parts.

discussion_questions: If a quarter means four equal parts, how many parts make up a whole?
Based on the source, how many counters are in one quarter of twelve?
lesson.content:
A quarter means taking one group of things and dividing it into four equal parts. When you have four equal parts together, each part is called a quarter.

If you have twelve counters, one quarter of those counters is three counters. This is because twelve divided into four equal groups gives you three in each group.

lesson.title: Understanding One Quarter

sections.title: What is a Quarter?
sections.content: One quarter is one of four equal parts of a whole. This means if you take one whole object and divide it into four pieces that are all the same size, each piece is called one quarter.

sections.title: Example with Counters
sections.content: To find one quarter of a group, you can divide the total number into four equal groups. For example, if you have twelve counters and divide them into four equal parts, one quarter is three counters.

lesson.summary: One quarter represents one out of four equal parts of a whole. In a group of twelve items, one quarter equals three items.

vocabulary.definition: Parts that are the same size or amount.
One of four equal parts of a whole.

discussion_questions: If you have twelve counters, how many counters make up one quarter?
How many equal parts do you need to make one quarter?
lesson.content:

To find one quarter of a group, you can divide the total number into four equal groups. For example, if you have twelve counters and divide them into four equal parts, one quarter is three counters.

lesson.title: Cup Observations

sections.title: Volume at Noon and One O'clock
sections.content: At noon, the cup held 70 mL of liquid. At one o'clock, the cup held 90 mL.

sections.title: The Change in Volume
sections.content: Between noon and one o'clock, 20 mL was added to the cup. This change resulted in the final amount of 90 mL (70 mL + 20 mL = 90 mL).

lesson.summary: The observations show that a cup started with 70 mL at noon and ended with 90 mL at one o'clock after 20 mL was added.

vocabulary.definition: A unit used to measure the amount of liquid in a container.

discussion_questions: How much liquid was in the cup at noon?
How much liquid was added between noon and one o'clock?
lesson.content:
At noon, the cup held 70 mL of liquid. At one o'clock, the cup held 90 mL.

Between noon and one o'clock, 20 mL was added to the cup. This change resulted in the final amount of 90 mL (70 mL + 20 mL = 90 mL).

[section:1]

lesson.title: Understanding Halves

sections.title: What is a Half?
sections.content: A half is one of two equal groups. When you put these two equal groups together, they make the whole collection.

sections.title: Example: Seeds
sections.content: Imagine a jar with eight seeds. If you split them into two equal groups, each group has four seeds. Therefore, half of eight seeds is four seeds.

lesson.summary: A half is one of two equal parts that make up a whole. For example, if you have eight seeds, half of that amount is four seeds.

vocabulary.definition: One of two equal groups that make a whole.
The entire collection or group.

discussion_questions: If you have eight seeds, how many are in one half?
What do the two equal groups make when you put them together?
objectives: Explain a half using simple words
lesson.content:
A half is one of two equal groups. When you put these two equal groups together, they make the whole collection.

Imagine a jar with eight seeds. If you split them into two equal groups, each group has four seeds. Therefore, half of eight seeds is four seeds.
